title: Uniform phase coverage gives small spot-dip error corrections in 118 TESS CPV stars
abstract: We reconstruct local spot-dip phase error covariance from released Fourier templates in 377 TESS sectors of 118 complex periodic variable stars. With uniform phase coverage, the median correction to the independently propagated relative-phase standard error is 1.000. The central 90 percent of star medians is 0.977 to 1.037. Reported spot-to-dip error ratios agree with Fisher predictions at a median ratio of 0.995. The correction changes a published Brownian drift-to-residual moment ratio from 0.150049 to 0.150070, far from one. Tests with every pair of missing phase bins give a median maximum correction of 1.079 and a largest correction of 1.287. Thus local fit coupling alone does not explain the Brownian consistency failure under uniform coverage. Fourier integration and independent linear-noise simulations check the method. The study does not determine material motion or lifetime. Unknown cadence weights, template error, shape evolution and correlations between chunks remain. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, exact input hashes and separate-scratch repeat instructions are included.

display.caption: Local phase error corrections under uniform phase coverage, the reported-to-predicted conditional error ratio, and the analytic dependence on Fisher correlation. The correction is small for most selected stars.

citations.reason: Released phase measurements, Fourier templates, fixed-dip controls and inspected conditional error code.
Reproduces the Brownian moment ratio and tests its sensitivity to reconstructed within-chunk phase error covariance.
Prior ordered covariance tests identify unknown spot-dip error covariance as a limit. This work reconstructs one local part of it.
Separate between-sector closure test; not reanalysed here.
